sections.title: Plan: secrets and delivery together
sections.html:
One plan for both designs. Org secrets come only from the parameter store; workspace secrets stay in the app database, and a workspace may use an org secret only when it is shared to it. Delivery uses one reply per request, with media inline and no duplicates.

#SliceOutcomeDepends on
S1Secret inventoryA table of every secret name (no values): scope, where stored, which agents use it, proposed home.-
S2Close the fallbackStored org values no longer reach every agent and agent-less session.-
S3Org catalogconfigs/org.yaml secrets with source: store and share.S1
S4Code ownersEvery PR requests the owner's review; no required-review rule.-
S5Move org secretsApproved names move to the store (a person writes values).S3, S4

Runs in parallel: S1, S2 and S4 start now; the chat and tracker adapters do not wait on secrets; only the code-host adapter waits for S5.

sections.title: Release assistant: agreed flow and the gates it checks before it posts
sections.html:
The assistant checks the gate at 09:00, posts the pre-release note, reminds assignees in the thread, and posts the go message once every box is ticked by a person.

  1. Gate check
  2. Pre-release note
  3. Reminder in the thread
  4. Go message

sections.title: Release assistant: message formats (agreed: styled, 1a-5a)
sections.html:
Format 1a

The pre-release note keeps one header line, the release name and the owner, then the changes as a short list. Long lists fold after five rows with a count of the rest.

sections.title: Intent and design
sections.html:
One streaming path replaces the batch job. Each record is validated, deduplicated and routed in a single handler, and every outbound notice goes through the provider wrapper with a signed receipt coming back.

In scope

  • Streaming validator and routing rules
  • Provider client, receipts, retry policy
  • Operator console with queue, failures and approvals

Out of scope

  • Customer-facing status page
  • Historical analytics beyond 90 days
  • Replacing the ticketing system

Flow

sections.title: Risks
sections.html:
RiskLikelihoodImpactMitigation
Provider outage longer than 10 minutesMediumHighFallback provider decision R1, quarterly drill
Dedup store fills faster than the TTL sweepLowMediumAlert at 80% capacity; sweep runs every minute
Sandbox credentials arrive lateHighMediumMock receipts locally; escalate through the needs list

Rollback

feature flag: intake.streaming = off   # falls back to the batch job within one cycle
restore routing rules: rules-loader --revision previous

decisions.rec: Stream, one record at a time, with a 5 s budget.
decisions.why: Batch windows delayed notices by up to 15 minutes, which broke the promised response time for the largest customer segment.
decisions.evidence: Replay of last month: 18% of records missed the old window; the streaming prototype met the budget on all of them.

decisions.rec: A keyed store with a 24 h TTL, not in the handler memory.
decisions.why: Handlers restart during deploys and in-memory state would let duplicates through for a few minutes each time.
decisions.evidence: Deploy log shows 9 restarts in two weeks; the memory approach produced 31 duplicates in the replay.

decisions.rec: Signed webhooks with a replay window of 5 minutes.
decisions.why: The provider rotates source addresses without notice; signatures survive that and cost one header check.
decisions.evidence: Provider docs section on delivery security; address list changed twice in the last quarter.
